query: Earlier efforts have produced HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations and have used thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and machine-learning modeling to identify promising alloys. However, large computational demands and low efficiency impede rapid discovery, while fracture properties such as toughness remain difficult to predict. For HfNbTiVAl10 in its reported hierarchical-heterostructured state, what single testable methodological hypothesis could overcome these limitations for predicting Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness under tensile and fracture testing? Explain the rationale, quantify the expected gains in accuracy and efficiency over prior methods, specify the conditions under which it would cease to be reliable, identify supporting prior evidence, and define a blinded prospective benchmark that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: For the hierarchically-heterostructured high-entropy alloy HfNbTiVAl10, an equivariant graph-neural-network (GNN) surrogate that is (i) pre-trained on ~20 000 inorganic-crystal elastic datasets and (ii) fine-tuned on ≤100 ab-initio calculations of representative local environments extracted from the alloy’s experimentally imaged nano- and micro-structures will predict the bulk Young’s modulus (E), 0.2 % offset yield strength (σy) and plane-strain fracture-toughness (KIC) with average absolute errors of ≤5 %, ≤10 % and ≤15 %, respectively, while reducing wall-clock computational cost by ≥100× relative to the current CALPHAD + hierarchical micro-mechanical simulation workflow.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTiVAl10 produced by vacuum arc-melting and homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h, followed by water quench, then cold-rolled 80 % and annealed 900 °C/1 h to obtain the reported hierarchical heterostructure (fcc+B2 nanoscale lamellae embedded in micron-scale fcc grains).
generation.intervention: Replace the existing property-prediction workflow with the proposed two-stage GNN surrogate: 1) generate <100 DFT datasets on 2–3 nm chemically decorated clusters cropped from TEM-derived 3D atom-probe reconstructions; 2) fine-tune a pre-trained equivariant GNN on these data and use the model to directly predict macroscopic E, σy and KIC.
generation.conditions: Room temperature (298 K) monotonic uniaxial tension at 10-3 s-1 until fracture, and compact-tension fracture tests per ASTM E1820; grain size 1–5 µm; lamellar spacing 10–50 nm; no secondary heat treatments.
generation.structural_mediator: Statistics of local chemical short-range order and phase boundaries captured in the 3D cluster graphs supplied to the GNN.
generation.mechanism: The pre-trained equivariant GNN embeds atomic environments so that elastic moduli are nearly linear in learned feature space; fine-tuning on a small, alloy-specific, high-fidelity dataset transfers this representation to the hierarchical alloy, allowing the network to integrate the distribution of local stiffnesses and cohesive energies into bulk mechanical responses without explicit micro-mechanical simulation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean absolute prediction errors relative to blinded experiments: |ΔE| ≤ 5 GPa (≈5 %), |Δσy| ≤ 80 MPa (≈10 %), |ΔKIC| ≤ 3 MPa·m1/2 (≈15 %). Wall-clock time from structure input to property prediction ≤2 CPU-hours (≥100× faster than the present ≳200 CPU-hours CALPHAD + phase-field + finite-element chain).
generation.baseline: Best-reported multiscale CALPHAD + phase-field + crystal-plasticity pipeline for the same alloy yielded errors of ~15 % in E, 25–30 % in σy, and >40 % in KIC with ≥200 CPU-h computation.
generation.boundary: Reliability falls if: 1) phase fractions deviate by >10 % from the training microstructure, 2) new intermetallic phases appear, 3) testing temperature differs by >150 K, or 4) grain/lamella dimensions exceed the largest clusters used for fine-tuning, breaking the locality assumption.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertain whether 100 DFT datapoints suffice to regress fracture-related quantities; size effects or rare defect-controlled failures may require additional physics-based constraints.

falsification_experiment.design: A blinded, prospective round-robin benchmark. Organizer supplies only atom-probe/TEM 3D reconstructions (no mechanical data) for three fresh HfNbTiVAl10 batches processed as specified. Participants deliver single-shot predictions of E, σy and KIC using the proposed GNN method. Organizer then measures the properties experimentally per stated conditions.
measurements: Yield strength from uniaxial tensile tests
Plane-strain fracture toughness (J→KIC) from compact-tension specimens
CPU-time and node-hours recorded for each prediction pipeline
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if either: a) any of the three target properties exceeds the stated error bounds for two or more of the three batches, or b) total computational cost exceeds 10 CPU-hours per batch for the surrogate prediction.
